claim: Day 20 of the 75 Hard Plus, Holistic Alpha Style challenge (explained in the episode of May 4th), all numbers hit: awesome so far, and definitely a challenge, as expected
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: One of the most effective ways found to change habits, personally and in coaching guys, is tracking them with tallies, on paper or, for most guys, in a phone app
Needless to say, tracking habits with tallies works, extremely well
We truly are the sum of our habits: who we are, what we experience, our life situation, in a lot of ways our identity, what we become and the life we build are largely determined by them
One of the best ways to upgrade our life, maybe one of the only ways, is to upgrade our habits
One of the best ways to upgrade our habits is tallies

A client that day mentioned briefly something actually pretty powerful: a cold shower felt like just part of who he is now, and he didn't really feel he needed to track it with a tally anymore. That is the process we want
To truly change our lives, change our habits so they become who we are
At first, a daily tally takes discipline and the system of tracking, which is highly effective: the system you use is everything here
At first, a daily tally takes thinking about it, intention, and setting up the situation to be easy and rewarding, your environment triggering the habit
A habit on a daily tally, executed long enough, becomes automatic, part of who you are

A habit going from tallied to automatic happened with a lot of things by now, certainly cold showers: once intentional and tracked, now automatic and untracked, one every day; never using a tally app again wouldn't matter
So often, it seems, we think a change (working out, cold showers, eating better, a sexual health thing) will always take a massive, constant effort
A change doesn't take the same effort forever: what takes effort is changing the habit, and once it's ingrained deeply enough it becomes automatic

Automatic now: cold showers, meditating, some workout every day, Kegels, a lot of things. Some stay tracked to be absolutely certain they get done, though even untracked, some things would still just get done, being a part of identity. Others in the current challenge aren't that automatic and mean pushing edges to stay on track, a great thing too: being willing and able to do that is an important part of growing
Reaching automatic with a habit is beautiful, because then you've truly changed who you are
A cold shower might not seem exciting, but the process that made it automatic is: if you can do that for one habit, you can do it for any other
Guaranteed, you have taken some habit to automatic, recently or further back: it became automatic, and even if it takes some effort it doesn't feel like a lot
Having taken some habit to automatic, guaranteed, you can do it again for any habit you choose: you own the process to make a habit part of your identity
Put the process to make a habit part of your identity to use where you want
The process of a habit: not happening at all, then happening with a system, tracking and intention, then automatic, who you are
The more we move positive things through the process from not happening to automatic, the more we change our life, period
Tracking habits does not need to be 18 things at a time, as mentioned before

After a long time with the system of tallies, about 20 things are tracked in the 75 Hard Plus challenge, a few already kind of automatic, some part of the actual rules, a lot not, partially to kind of prove how much the system works
Don't track 20 things. Start with one, every single day, making sure it gets done every single day, or maybe two or three
His son tracks three habits right now: water, push-ups and squats
Once used to tallies, expand: a habit goes from not existing, to your tally, to automatic, then off the tally to make room for another
Over time which one, two or three habits you tally change, and maybe you add some
With a system to track habits day to day, a tally app or not, you have the power to take anything from absent, to present with effort and tracking, to automatic, a good place for habits to be
Your habits determine who you become and your life path: pay attention to them and upgrade them
